  # kill with no diagnosis. The budget/stall watchdog built to catch that
  # faster could not tell a zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job
  # legitimately occupying the shared fa-m5-1 (its own comment admitted
  # it), and its 31m stall window did not cover the cli sibling chain's
  # 335m worst-case — so it false-cancelled healthy queues by design
  # (gh-1903, #1735). The zombie goal is now met by the bounds above plus
  # the leg-timeout orphan-cancel diagnostic, not by a heuristic that
  # cannot tell a queue from a zombie.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120); 360m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. The 360m cap
    # also bounds any gh-172 zombie wait — on leg timeout the watcher's
    # orphan-cancel kills only this leg's never-started child (gh-1903).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # No inputs to disambiguate on (newest-in-tight-window
          # fallback); the wait is bounded by the office-addin-suite
          # job's own 45m timeout (#344) and this leg's 150m — never by a
          # watcher cancel.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    # gh-1906: route to the shared `macos-m5` POOL. The gh-1692 pin of the
    # ONE known-good box (`fa-m5-1` runner-name label) is dead — no m5
    # runner carries a runner-name label anymore, so a set containing one
    # matched ZERO runners and both iOS legs queued forever (live
    # 2026-10-26, blocked v1.0.648 TestFlight). The gh-1692 fa-m5-2
    # signing-env concern is retired: fa-m5-2/fa-m5-3 signed desktop green.
    # The generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64] list stays banned (gh-1600
    # F-A: it also matches the Linux box) — see
    # test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart, which audits this exact
    # label set and bans `fa-m5-*` name labels repo-wide.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

      # gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on this persistent box is SHARED across
      # workflow runs — the old bare workspace rm -rf failed the checkout on
      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # EXACT patch pin (gh-1826; #1431 discipline — the same 3.47.7 the
      # desktop lane pins): a wildcard spec (3.47.x) re-resolves a freshly
      # released patch the fa-m5 runners have not cached — run 40066130883
      # (2026-10-24) resolved 3.47.x to 3.47.8 and the TestFlight leg died
      # downloading the 2.27 GB SDK inside the bounded curl budget
      # (600s/attempt, 900s total) with 1.48 GB received. 3.47.7 already
      # sits in the persistent slot on every fa-m5 runner (zero download).
      # The runner's hardcoded $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4,
      # below the repo floor >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260). Bump the pin
      # consciously, matching the desktop lane, in the same PR as any
      # floor reseed.
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1692 AC2: the iOS lane pins xcbeautify as the xcodebuild
      # formatter (xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" —
      # the 10-17/10-18 archive failures printed NO error line). Homebrew
      # keeps it a one-time install on this persistent runner; the step
      # verifies the binary so a missing formatter can never silently
      # re-introduce the xcpretty class.
      - name: Install xcbeautify (xcodebuild formatter, gh-1692)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v xcbeautify >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "xcbeautify already installed: $(xcbeautify --version)"
          else
            brew install xcbeautify
          fi
          xcbeautify --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no
      # retry. The bounded retry + deterministic-skew fail-fast now lives
      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in
      # the repo rides (gh-1310; pinned by test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
      # test.dart).
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # NOTE: no percent-decoding of the file: URI — pub-cache paths on
          # this runner carry no URI escapes; add unquoting if that changes.
          JS_WR=$(python3 -c '
            import json, pathlib
            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
            p = next((q for q in cfg["packages"] if q["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"), None)
            print(p["rootUri"] if p else "")
          ')
          if [ -z "$JS_WR" ]; then
            echo "::warning::js_widget_runtime not in package_config.json — no fixture to prune, skipping"
            exit 0
          fi
          case "$JS_WR" in
            file://*) JS_WR=${JS_WR#file://} ;;
          esac
          case "$JS_WR" in
            /*) ;;
            *) JS_WR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$JS_WR" ;;
          esac
          GLB="$JS_WR/test/assets/coach_anny.glb"
          if [ -f "$GLB" ]; then
            rm -f "$GLB"
            echo "pruned coach_anny.glb (5.6 MB never-loaded test fixture, #1331) from $JS_WR"
          else
            echo "coach_anny.glb already absent — nothing to prune"
          fi

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "Local framework not found, downloading from upstream release..."
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56) —
            # the run-34709113737 failure: reset 3s into the 92.7 MB asset.
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
              https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - name: Validate iOS secrets
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_PASSWORD" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_PASSWORD secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All required iOS secrets are present"

      - name: Provision signing via ci-sign (persistent host keychain)
        id: ios_signing
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: IOS_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: IOS_P12_PASSWORD
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1865: the repo copy of ci-sign is authoritative —
          # re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so
          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          # gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28): NO per-job
          # keychains and NO user-global keychain writes. ~/bin/ci-sign
          # provisions the PERSISTENT ci-signing.keychain-db (idempotent —
          # a re-run with the same certificate is a no-op), resolves the
          # identity by SHA-1 (never the generic name — the additive
          # search list can hold a concurrent leg's same-subject
          # certificate, run 40455401630), and never triggers interactive
          # keychain prompts (partition list set at install).
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_BASE64 secret is not set — cannot sign"
            exit 1
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-ios
          IOS_CERT_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-ios)
          IOS_CERT_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-ios)
          echo "identity_sha1=$IOS_CERT_SHA1" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "identity_name=$IOS_CERT_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "gh-1865: signing identity pinned by SHA-1: $IOS_CERT_NAME ($IOS_CERT_SHA1)"

          mkdir -p ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles
          echo "$IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/profile.mobileprovision

          # The FaLiveActivity extension signs MANUALLY too (the runner's
          # Xcode has no Apple account, so -allowProvisioningUpdates cannot
          # create profiles). Its App Store profile rides its own secret.
          if [ -n "$IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/liveactivity.mobileprovision
          else
            echo "::error::IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64 secret is not set (App Store profile for dev.fa1.app.FaLiveActivity)"
            exit 1
          fi

          # gh-1865 fail-fast precheck (option B): every profile must embed
          # the provisioned certificate. A mismatch aborts in seconds,
          # BEFORE the ~24-minute archive (run 40455519923 died at gym on
          # BOTH targets). Decoding goes through ci-sign plist —
          # `security cms -D` needs a default keychain, which the
          # persistent-keychain model does not set (default-keychain
          # writes are user-global state, part of the retired model).
          ~/bin/ci-sign doctor ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/profile.mobileprovision fa-ios
          ~/bin/ci-sign doctor ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/liveactivity.mobileprovision fa-ios

      - name: Ensure iOS device SDK is available
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Available iOS SDKs:"
          xcodebuild -showsdks | grep iphoneos || true
          echo "Downloading iOS platform if missing..."
          xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS || true
          # The attached device may run a newer iOS than the installed SDK;
          # try to download the matching version. If this fails, the build
          # will still fail with a clearer message.
          xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS -buildVersion 26.5 || true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The plist is gitignored, so the fresh CI checkout has none and the
      # native Firebase SDK logs I-COR000012/0008 at startup. Inject it from
      # a secret when available (same dev.fa1.app registration as
      # firebase_options.dart).
      - name: Write GoogleService-Info.plist (iOS)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist
            echo "GoogleService-Info.plist written (bundle: $(plutil -extract BUNDLE_ID raw flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 not set — building without the native Firebase plist"
          fi

      - name: Build iOS IPA
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          # Issue #726 (run 35564638018): ASC closed the 1.0.0 train once a
          # 1.0.0 build was approved (error 90186) and rejects new builds
          # whose CFBundleShortVersionString is not higher than the
          # previously approved version (error 90062) — pubspec pins 1.0.0,
          # so the daily train stalled forever. Ship the derived next-tag
          # version (e.g. 0.1.446), which strictly increases.
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          # gh-1865: CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY as a SHA-1 fingerprint (read from
          # THIS job's own keychain right after import) instead of the
          # generic "iPhone Distribution" — a concurrent signing leg's
          # same-CN cert in the shared additive search list can no longer
          # shadow the identity at codesign time.
          IOS_CERT_SHA1: ${{ steps.ios_signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
          bundle install

          PROFILE=~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/profile.mobileprovision
          # gh-1865 model v3: profile decoding via ci-sign plist —
          # `security cms -D` requires a default keychain and the
          # persistent-keychain model never sets one (default-keychain
          # writes are user-global state, part of the retired model).
          UUID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist "$PROFILE" | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
          TEAM_ID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist "$PROFILE" | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw -)
          BUNDLE_ID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist "$PROFILE" | plutil -extract Entitlements.application-identifier raw - | sed "s/^$TEAM_ID.//")
          PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist "$PROFILE" | plutil -extract Name raw -)
          echo "PROFILE_NAME=$PROFILE_NAME"

          LA_PROFILE=~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/liveactivity.mobileprovision
          LA_PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist "$LA_PROFILE" | plutil -extract Name raw -)
          echo "LA_PROFILE_NAME=$LA_PROFILE_NAME"

          IOS_TEAM_ID="$TEAM_ID" \
          IOS_BUNDLE_ID="$BUNDLE_ID" \
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME="$PROFILE_NAME" \
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_NAME="$LA_PROFILE_NAME" \
          IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY="$IOS_CERT_SHA1" \
          bundle exec fastlane ios build_only

      # gh-1692 AC2: the gym log holds the REAL xcodebuild error — without
      # this artifact an archive failure was undiagnosable from GitHub (the
      # log lived only ON the runner; xcpretty printed no error line). The
      # lane also dumps the newest log tail into the job log on failure;
      # this artifact is the full-fidelity copy. Failure-gated so green
      # runs upload nothing.
      - name: Upload gym logs on archive failure (gh-1692)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 size diet: the exported IPA ships ~99 MB (uncompressed) of
      # debug dSYMs under Symbols/. App Store Connect strips that directory
      # from device delivery anyway (TestFlight reports ~157 MB — the
      # payload WITHOUT Symbols), so it is dead weight in the artifact.
      # Repack without it: Payload/ is untouched (codesign validity lives
      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1403: absolutize BEFORE the rezip — find yields a RELATIVE
          # path, and the `(cd "$STRIP" && …)` subshell resolved
          # "$IPA_PATH.stripped" against the mktemp dir (no flutter_app/
          # ancestor) → "zip error: Could not create output file". The
          # atomic-swap mv below carried the same hazard.
          # (realpath: /usr/bin/realpath, macOS 13+ — the runner is newer.)
          IPA_PATH=$(realpath "$IPA_PATH")
          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
            exit 0
          fi
          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$STRIP"' EXIT
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          # Atomic swap: the original IPA survives a failed rezip (the
          # un-stripped copy still beats no artifact for debugging).
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH.stripped" {} +)
          mv -f "$IPA_PATH.stripped" "$IPA_PATH"
          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact
        # Uploaded before the symbol gate so a failed gate still leaves the
        # IPA available for debugging.
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/*.ipa
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 ratchet: per-file uncompressed floor seeded from the last
      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL fails the leg — same gate
      # family as the macOS pass (#1227). Eviction is pinned separately by
      # the --forbid deny-list: the NEW-line guard alone only catches
      # re-adds above 5% of TOTAL (Symbols/ qualifies at 99 MB; the 5.6 MB
      # glb does not — +3.8% TOTAL, sub-share NEW), so a returning evicted
      # artifact fails via --forbid in the same step. Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime always ships (the on-device
      # LiteRT LM keep-set ended with the gemma stack removal — gh-2004).
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$MANIFEST"' EXIT
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv \
            --forbid '^Symbols/' --forbid 'coach_anny\.glb$' \
            --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1
            }
          done
          echo "✅ wasm runtime keep-set present; iOS size ratchet green"

      - name: Verify IPA and FFI symbols
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "IPA built successfully: $(ls -la "$IPA_PATH")"

          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$CHECK_DIR"
          PLIST=$(echo "$CHECK_DIR"/Payload/*.app/Info.plist)
          EXEC_NAME=$(plutil -extract CFBundleExecutable raw "$PLIST")
          BIN="$(dirname "$PLIST")/$EXEC_NAME"
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

          # cupertino_http trampolines (_NativeCupertinoHttp_*) live in a
          # static pod framework nothing native references; without the
          # Podfile force_load the Release link drops them and every network
          # call fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found'). Gate on it here so a
          # broken IPA never reaches TestFlight again.
          CUPERTINO_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " __NativeCupertinoHttp_" || true)
          echo "cupertino_http _NativeCupertinoHttp_* exports in binary: $CUPERTINO_COUNT"
          if [ "$CUPERTINO_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols exported from the app binary — networking via NSURLSession would fail at runtime"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ cupertino_http FFI symbols are exported"
          rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR"

      - name: Cleanup
        if: always()
        run: |
          # gh-1865 model v3: no per-job keychain to clean up — the
          # persistent ci-signing keychain is host state, never deleted
          # from jobs. Only the decoded p12 scratch file goes.
          rm -f certificate.p12

  submit-ios:
    name: Submit iOS to TestFlight
    needs: [build-ios]
    # gh-1906: same shared `macos-m5` pool as build-ios above — the gh-1692
    # fa-m5-1 name pin is dead (no runner carries a name label; the set
    # matched zero runners and queued forever). The generic [self-hosted,
    # macOS, ARM64] list stays banned (gh-1600 F-A: it also matches the
    # Linux box).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #344 wedge bound + #351 arithmetic: the submit_only lane waits
    # for Apple processing (TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 5400s
    # = 90m — a healthy slow ASC processing is NOT a wedge); distribution
    # appearance is verified by the DEFERRED store-appearance-check
    # workflow (gh-1041 — a single non-failing probe runs after the upload,
    # the 900s wait-loop is gone). Job ceiling must exceed the lane worst
    # case:
    #   ~5m setup (mirror clone + artifact + bundle install)
    # + ~10m IPA upload to ASC
    # + 90m wait_processing_timeout_duration
    # + ~1m one-shot appearance probe
    # = 120m. The old 45m killed healthy slow submits mid-wait (the exact
    # failure #351 was filed for); a genuinely wedged job is still bounded
    # server-side at 120m, and the daily testflight watch budget (240m)
    # covers the whole version→build-ios(90)→submit-ios(120) chain.
    timeout-minutes: 120
    if: needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout (see build-ios) — the bare
      # workspace rm -rf must never fail this checkout on stale unremovable
      # leftovers in the persistent shared workspace. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box that is the PREVIOUS
      # run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Download IPA artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/ipa/

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      - name: Upload IPA to TestFlight
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          # External TestFlight distribution (issue #239): lanes fail
          # loudly when these are unset — set them once as repo variables.
          TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP: ${{ vars.TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP }}
          BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE }}
          # Must match the IPA's marketing version (BUILD_NAME of the build
          # job, issue #726) — verify_external_distribution! selects the
          # uploaded build by app version.
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::App Store Connect API key not configured — skipping TestFlight upload (the IPA stays on the GitHub release / artifacts)."
            exit 0
          fi
          IPA_PATH="$(find "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/flutter_app/ipa" -name '*.ipa' -type f | head -1)"
          echo "Uploading $IPA_PATH to TestFlight..."
          IOS_IPA_PATH="$IPA_PATH" bundle exec fastlane ios submit_only

  release-mobile:
    name: Create Mobile GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-android, build-android-apks, build-ios]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: |
      always() &&
      ((needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'skipped')) &&
      (needs.build-ios.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'skipped')
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the probe
      # itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers GH_TOKEN, which
      # every mint-reachable call site exports), so this grant matters
      # only if the probe is ever switched to the job token.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Nothing to release
        # Both platforms picked a no-binary content mode (none /
        # metadata_only / screenshots_only) — nothing was built, so there
        # is nothing to download or release. Record it in the job summary
        # and skip every release step instead of failing on `ls artifacts/`.
        if: needs.build-android.result != 'success' && needs.build-android-apks.result != 'success' && needs.build-ios.result != 'success'
        run: |
          {
            echo '### Nothing to release'
            echo '`android_content` and `ios_content` both selected no binary build (none / metadata_only / screenshots_only) — no release created.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Checkout repository
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: release_notes.sh falls back to "commits since the
          # previous tag" when the CHANGELOG has no section for this version.
          # gh-1477: blobless — the notes read commit MESSAGES, never
          # historical file blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Download iOS IPA artifact
        if: needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download Android AAB artifact
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download store APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-store
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download god APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-god
          path: artifacts/

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        run: ls -laR artifacts/

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          AAB=$(find artifacts -name "*.aab" -type f | head -1)
          IPA=$(find artifacts -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          STORE_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-store-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          GOD_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-god-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          echo "AAB: $AAB"
          echo "IPA: $IPA"
          echo "store APK: $STORE_APK"
          echo "god APK: $GOD_APK"

          ASSETS=()
          [ -n "$AAB" ] && ASSETS+=("$AAB")
          [ -n "$IPA" ] && ASSETS+=("$IPA")
          [ -n "$STORE_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$STORE_APK")
          [ -n "$GOD_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$GOD_APK")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **Android**: Download the AAB and upload to Play Store, or use `flutter install`.\n- **Android god flavor (sideload only)**: install the god APK directly — see https://fa1.dev/android.\n- **iOS**: Download the IPA and upload to TestFlight via Xcode or Transporter.\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG from the macOS build workflow.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the macOS leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: >-
          always() && job.status != 'success' &&
          (needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success')
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults

    The daily build-macos attach resolves latest+1 at dispatch; the sibling
    train (mobile leg draft + minted tag -> tag CI -> provenance publish) can
    publish that tag while the serialized self-hosted mac builds are still
    running (v1.0.685: draft 05:22:46Z, published 05:44:52Z, mac leg attached
    06:28:53Z). release_asset_gate.sh then refuses the unattached fa-* assets
    (gh-2042 AC1 — correct) and the leg red-fails, auto-filing a daily ticket
    and discarding the desktop build.
    
    Give the gate an explicit caller-declared pre-stage policy:
    RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1 turns the PUBLISHED+unattached-fa-* verdict
    into a loud whole-call skip (::warning::, exit 0, nothing uploaded, no
    twin create, no flip — all-or-nothing, so latest-mac.yml can never land
    alone on a release whose zips were skipped). The default stays the loud
    refusal; only build-macos.yml's release-macos attach step opts in. The
    CLI-tar and extension attaches keep the refusal (they carry REQUIRED
    release assets the tag train ships).
    
    Tests: gate-level policy verdicts (skip, mixed whole-call, draft
    untouched, opt-in discipline), attach-or-create end-to-end (green leg,
    zero mutation), workflow env pin; all existing gh-2042 pins untouched.
